e66df9845a.q: Should an optometrist buy or lease a building when opening a new practice?
e66df9845a.a: Gurpreet Lika advises optometrists to pursue owning their own building rather than leasing, as it provides long-term asset growth and allows them to retain the real estate even if they sell the practice later. He took 15 years to achieve this goal, but believes the advantages of ownership—including being able to retire and still collect rent from the strata—make it worth the investment and effort.

e23266b333.q: What location factors should optometrists evaluate when opening a new practice?
e23266b333.a: Key location factors include proximity to existing practices (Gurpreet's new location is an eight-minute drive from Royal Look Optometry), neighborhood affluence and patient demographics (he chose the second highest-end neighborhood in Victoria), and whether it's a place you'd be willing to drive to in 10-15 years regardless of where you live. The location should also accommodate overflow from existing practices and serve as a backup plan in case primary office developments occur.

2e9cf0bb6c.q: How does office aesthetics and design affect patient spending in an optometry practice?

Gurpreet observed that when the same patients and doctors are in a newly renovated, modern space versus an older facility, patients in the new location spend considerably more on eyewear. After six months, the new oceanfront practice already shows higher average sales per patient, suggesting that aesthetic elevation increases patient willingness to spend on premium products.
